Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern directly implements Cloneable interface. (SING_SINGLETON_IMPLEMENTS_CLONEABLE)
Bug_Details:
If a class using singleton design pattern directly implements the Cloneable interface, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
Therefore, implementing the Cloneable interface should be avoided.

For more information, see: SEI CERT MSC07-J.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded by having the SingletonBug class implement the Cloneable interface. This allows the creation of a cloned instance of the singleton, which violates the singleton pattern's principle of having only one instance.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by attempting to clone a singleton instance. The first test method explicitly calls the clone method on the singleton instance, expecting a CloneNotSupportedException to be thrown. The second test method calls the showBug method, which internally attempts to clone the singleton instance, causing the test to fail.
